html:
SMTO-GML-0037 — Google couldn't find that Gmail item

GUID: bf160630-2846-4e74-8607-2c02e3135a17
Slug: gmail-provider-resource-missing
Domain: GML · Subsystem: gml

What happened

  • The email, draft, label or attachment SMTO asked for isn't in this Gmail account anymore, or it belongs to a different account. Nothing was changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Gmail in your browser and check that the item still exists in that account and isn't in Trash. If it was deleted or moved, Google can't return it.
  2. In the conversation, ask SMTO to search for it again and name the account, for example 'Find the latest email from alice@example.com in @work_gmail'. A new search gives SMTO the item's current reference instead of an outdated one.
  3. Then ask SMTO to do the action on the item it just found. Using the fresh result avoids pointing at something that changed in the meantime.

What success looks like

  • SMTO finds the item and completes the action on it.

If it still fails

  • If Gmail shows the item but SMTO still can't find it, select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO, saying which account and email you meant.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Google returned HTTP 404 for the requested Gmail resource, and no more specific resource cause was recorded.

What this means

  • The typed Gmail API resolver receives numeric status 404 and no stronger resource-specific cause. Gmail provider receipts and exact account/message identities determine effects. Authorization, pagination or presentation failure cannot undo a send or other mutation; diagnostic rendering performs no mailbox or OAuth request.

Why this can happen

  • The typed Gmail API resolver receives numeric status 404 and no stronger resource-specific cause.

How to diagnose it

  • Refresh the intended account's resource listing and verify exact resource identity/ownership.

How to fix it

  • The message, draft, label or attachment ID does not exist in the selected account (deleted, replaced, or taken from another account). Re-list or search the intended account to obtain a current ID, confirm account_ref matches the mailbox the ID came from, and resubmit with the fresh identifier rather than the stale one.
  • Refresh the intended account’s resource listing and select a current message, draft, label or attachment identity. Confirm the account and resource scope before another request.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • A current authorized message/draft/label/attachment reference resolves in the intended account.

What not to do

  • Do not submit a stale identifier or revision after another actor changed the resource.

Technical notes

  • Gmail provider receipts and exact account/message identities determine effects. Authorization, pagination or presentation failure cannot undo a send or other mutation; diagnostic rendering performs no mailbox or OAuth request.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
